report.tagline: A finance app from Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal that offers UPI payments, personal and home loans, health insurance and low-cost mutual funds.
report.simpleSummary: Navi is one app for paying, borrowing, saving and insuring. People mostly come for UPI payments with cashback, then get offered a personal loan or a cheap mutual fund. Navi makes most of its money from the interest on loans. It keeps prices low to win users, and makes it back when some of them borrow.

overview.whatItDoes: Navi is a consumer finance app founded in 2018 by Sachin Bansal and Ankit Agarwal. It offers UPI payments, instant personal loans, home loans, loans against property, health insurance and index mutual funds. Lending is done by its own NBFC, Navi Finserv. It uses UPI as the daily habit that brings users in, then sells them loans and other products.
howItWorks: User installs the app, links a bank account and starts paying by UPI, often with cashback.
Navi studies usage and credit data to pre-approve personal loans.
Loans are approved and paid out in minutes, fully online with Aadhaar and PAN.
Users repay via UPI AutoPay or bank mandates.
Navi also sells low-fee index funds and health insurance in the same app.
A credit line on UPI lets users borrow small amounts while paying.
overview.valueProposition: Cheap and fast financial products in one simple app. Free UPI with rewards, loans in minutes without paperwork, and some of the lowest-cost index funds in India.

businessModel.summary: Navi makes most of its money from interest on loans, mainly personal loans. UPI, cheap mutual funds and insurance are ways to get and keep users, so they can later be offered loans.

revenueStreams.detail: Interest and fees on personal, home and property loans through Navi Finserv.
Health insurance through Navi General Insurance.
Small management fees on index funds.
Almost no direct revenue; a cost due to cashback.

businessModel.pricing: Personal loan rates are set per user based on credit; index funds have very low fees; UPI is free for users.
costDrivers: Interest Navi pays to borrow money (₹1,123 crore in FY26)
Marketing and cashback for UPI (other expenses up 80% to ₹1,112 crore)
Bad loans (₹408 crore impairment in FY26)
businessModel.unitEconomics: Take a ₹1 lakh personal loan at about 18% a year. Navi earns about ₹18,000 interest in a year. It pays maybe ₹9,000 to ₹10,000 on its own borrowing, sets aside a few thousand for defaults, and spends on getting and serving the customer. If the user came through UPI, the acquisition cost is spread across many cheap UPI users, most of whom never borrow. So the model works only if enough UPI users become good borrowers. Numbers are estimates.

howTheyGetUsers: App store ads and digital marketing
whatBringsUsersBack: New loan offers after good repayment
growth.moat: Combines high-frequency UPI with its own lending licence. Few UPI apps have their own NBFC, and few lenders have daily user activity. This gives Navi cheap users and payment data to judge credit.

northStar.metric: Monthly users who complete at least one financial action (payment, repayment, SIP or claim) on Navi
northStar.why: Shows Navi is part of users' money lives. Active users are the base for safe lending.

strengths: Fast growth in UPI and users
Own NBFC with good asset quality
Profit before tax turned positive in Q4 FY26
weaknesses: 92% of assets in risky personal loans
Loss widened in FY26 due to UPI spending
Depends on Sachin Bansal's capital and brand
risks: RBI action on lending prices (Navi Finserv was barred from new loans for some weeks in late 2024 over pricing)
UPI market share caps and rules
Competition from big UPI apps lending
userComplaints: High interest rates on personal loans

improvementIdeas.idea: Show total cost of loan in rupees before acceptance
Smart rewards that drop for heavy users and rise for new ones
Respectful repayment reminders with easy reschedule option
Grow secured lending like home loans

pmLessons: A free, frequent product (UPI) can bring users cheaply, but must lead to a paid product.
Low prices can grow fast but burn cash; watch the path to profit.
In lending, growth is easy; repayment is the real test.
Regulation can stop a product overnight, so build in compliance.

interviewQuestions.question: Is UPI cashback a good growth strategy for Navi?
interviewQuestions.hint: Compare cashback cost with lifetime value from loans. Look at how many UPI users borrow and repay.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce personal loan defaults?
interviewQuestions.hint: Better credit scoring with UPI data, lower first loan limits, reminders and early help for stressed users.

interviewQuestions.question: What is Navi's north star metric?
interviewQuestions.hint: Monthly users completing a financial action. Break into UPI, lending, quality and cross-sell.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you cross-sell insurance to loan users?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find the moment of need, like after a loan, offer a simple plan, measure attach rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Navi focus on fewer products?
interviewQuestions.hint: Weigh focus against cross-sell benefits. Use data on which products drive profit.
